tagline: 3,260 kilometres of coast, two great deltas, a thousand karst islands — a country that faces the sea.
summary: Vietnam runs more than 3,260 kilometres down the South China Sea, anchored by the Red River and Mekong deltas and studded with destinations that are reached best by water — Ha Long Bay's karst islands, Phú Quốc, Nha Trang's bays, and the Da Nang–Hoi An–Cham Island coast. Its tourism and coastal economy are booming, but the water tier is still slow junk-boats and conventional ferries. A clean foiling layer fits Vietnam's coast as naturally as anywhere in Asia.
why_marine_mobility: Vietnam's signature experiences are on the water — the karst seascape of Ha Long Bay, the island of Phú Quốc, the Cham Islands off Hoi An. Today these run on slow, diesel junk-boats and ferries. Navier's Pioneer II turns the coastal and island hops into fast, smooth, clean crossings, and the booming Da Nang–Hoi An corridor is a ready-made first beachhead for an in-app sea tier.

demand_signals.label: Coastal-tourism boom
demand_signals.note: Ha Long Bay, Phú Quốc, Nha Trang and the Da Nang–Hoi An coast are among Asia's fastest-growing leisure destinations, each dependent on a water leg.

demand_signals.label: Ride-hail depth
demand_signals.note: Grab and Gojek operate at scale across Vietnamese cities — an in-app sea tier extends a proven demand curve onto the coast.

demand_signals.label: Delta & island geography
demand_signals.note: The Mekong and Red River deltas plus offshore islands make water a core part of regional movement, not an afterthought.

use_cases.body: Da Nang / Hoi An to the Cham Islands: a fast, clean foiling hop into a UNESCO biosphere reserve, replacing the slow ferry on Vietnam's most dynamic tourism coast.
Ha Long Bay: a smooth, low-wake foiling tier threading the karst islands — quieter and cleaner than the diesel junk-boat fleet (aspirational corridor, pending boarding points).
Phú Quốc: fast island access for Vietnam's flagship resort island (aspirational corridor, pending boarding points).

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The Da Nang–Hoi An–Cham Island coast and Ha Long Bay's island hops sit well inside Pioneer II's 70-nautical-mile range at 30 knots — commercial-ready today.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Longer coastal trunks linking major bays and the offshore islands become Quanta-LR territory (~700 nm hybrid range, H2 2026+) as the network extends.

signature_routes.label: Da Nang / Hoi An ↔ Cham Islands — the live coastal hop
Ha Long Bay — karst-island foiling tier (aspirational, pending boarding points)
Phú Quốc — flagship resort-island access (aspirational, pending boarding points)

transit_planning: For an authority or super-app operator: a clean, fast water tier that upgrades Vietnam's signature coastal and island journeys from slow diesel boats to smooth foiling crossings. Start on the proven Da Nang–Hoi An–Cham coast with Pioneer II, then extend to Ha Long Bay and Phú Quốc as boarding points and range come online.
competitive_landscape: Coastal and island travel today runs on diesel junk-boats and conventional ferries — atmospheric but slow, noisy and carbon-heavy. Navier's foiling tier is faster, smoother, cleaner and in-app — the modern layer over a tourism coast that is growing faster than its water infrastructure.
regulatory_note: Maritime transport is overseen by the Vietnam Maritime Administration (Vinamarine) under the Ministry of Transport; passenger operation in protected areas such as Ha Long Bay and the Cham Islands biosphere also intersects provincial and conservation authorities.
seasonality: The dry season varies by region — Nov–Apr in the north (Ha Long), Feb–Aug in the centre (Da Nang/Hoi An), and Nov–Apr in the south (Phú Quốc); typhoon season (Jul–Nov) brings rougher seas to the central and northern coasts.

precedents.what: Four Seasons Lake Austin operates an N30 in live luxury-hospitality service — proof of the premium clean water-shuttle model Navier brings to coastal markets.
